In today's class I asked students for creative examples of externalities.

The winner: Getting a tattoo is a negative consumption externality because it raises the chances a cannibal decides to spare you and eat the person next to you instead.

You don’t have to love powerlooms or hate hand weaving to recognize a powerloom when you see one.

Lots of intellectual tasks that used to be pure craft & which, therefore, could never be industrialized might soon be subject to the logic of industrialization. Not an easy change.
